newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: New Afghan rulers order prayers five times a day.
newsitem.headline: New Afghan rulers order prayers five times a day.

text.p: The radical Taleban militia that conquered Afghanistan last week has ordered people to offer Islamic prayers five times a day as its latest measure to enforce a purist brand of Islam.

A broadcast by the Taleban-controlled Kabul Radio on Tuesday night, whose report was available on Wednesday, quoted a religious department official as asking local prayer leaders and headmen to bring violators to Taleban offices.

Since conquering the capital Kabul on Friday, the Taleban has barred women from leaving their homes without the Islamic "hejab" veil and from working in offices, and told men to grow long beards within a month and a half.

The decrees by the Taleban, which began as a movement of theology students and now controls three quarters of the country, have struck fear into many educated people, especially women, in the Afghan capital.
Taleban had earlier decreed death by stoning for adultery and amputation of hands for theft.

But in a rare show of leniency after an outcry abroad about the denial of women's rights, Taleban's supreme leader Mullah Mohammad Omar issued a decree on Monday promising women laid off from their jobs to be paid their salaries without working.
Their salaries will be sent to their homes, a Kabul Radio broadcast said on Tuesday.

The Tuesday night announcement said the Department for the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice "draws the attention of the people to the observance of prayer five times a day and to invite forsakers to observe this duty."
"Those who do not perform the prayer in fact are committing a grave sin and those who reject it are infidels," it said.

"Therefore, all mosque preachers, village headmen and local elders are hereby instructed to bring those who forsake prayer to the nearest office of the Taleban movement for the implementation of Shariah order," the broadcast said.
It did not specify the punishment for not praying, which a Moslem must do at Fajr (early morning), Zuhr (midday), Asr (afternoon), Maghreb (evening), and Isha (night).
"We request our faithful brothers to do their best to perform their prayer collectively in mosques," it said.
The radio said it had been told by the Taleban's acting head of security in Kabul, Mullah Fazel Ahmad Akhond, that "satisfactory security has been restored" in the city.
"No one is able to violate the property or honour of anyone. And profiteers or hoarders can no longer continue their illegitimate actions," Akhond was quoted as saying.
He said 85 "thieves and plunderers" had been caught over the past three days and that they were "undergoing legal and Sharia investigation."

Also, 90 motor vehicles belonging to the government or to private individuals had been confiscated and handed over to the relevant authorities or to the original owners, he said. Five hundred weapons had also been confiscated.
